claim: Finite software checks in progress; no external empirical or operational assurance.

findings.exploit: A controller selects a hidden favorable model, ledger or frontier instead of a common observation policy.
findings.correction: Retain correlated fixed-model full-ledger supports and reconstruct every visible branch independently.

findings.exploit: A paid probe is compared against an unmatched or incompletely optimized information baseline.
findings.correction: Reoptimize paid-but-masked and no-sensing classes separately; incomplete results remain unknown.

findings.exploit: A composite bypasses interior costs, primitive limits, evidence admission or execution authority.
findings.correction: Unfold finite typed IR over every adverse primitive branch, charge formation/use and recheck domain-bound certificates.

findings.exploit: Replanning changes an entry comparison epoch or resets synthesis work and existing ledger obligations.
findings.correction: Bind the entry comparison checkpoint in visible history, replay accumulated cost events and reserve maximum synthesis expansions.

findings.exploit: Individually compatible symbols and recorded ledger projections may have no common fixed-model history.
findings.correction: Reconstruct a bounded joint receipt/ledger/kernel trace; reject contradiction while preserving the full visible-only controller support.

findings.exploit: A mutation score can omit decorated control classes or import original nested packages instead of their mutated copies.
findings.correction: Use undecorated control classes, copy hash-identical sources into one mutation import layout, assert baseline import origins and reject incomplete module/method scope separately from execution and score gates.
